options.a: Tasks, KSAs, and working conditions
options.b: Pay grades and market salary benchmarks
options.c: Performance ratings for current incumbents
options.d: Personality traits of top hires

distractorExplanations.b: Pay grades and benchmarks come from job evaluation and market pricing, which use job analysis output but are not its product.
distractorExplanations.c: Performance ratings describe how incumbents perform; job analysis describes the job itself, independent of who holds it.
distractorExplanations.d: Job analysis studies the job, not people; trait profiles of top performers invite non-job-related selection criteria.

options.a: A legally allowed race or color requirement when customers prefer it
options.b: An age limit an employer may set whenever it lowers training costs
options.c: A legally allowed sex/religion/national-origin requirement essential to the job
options.d: A neutral job requirement justified by business necessity in a disparate impact case

distractorExplanations.a: Title VII allows no BFOQ for race or color, and customer preference is not a valid BFOQ basis.
distractorExplanations.b: Age BFOQs under the ADEA are narrow (e.g., public safety); lower training cost is not a lawful basis.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses BFOQ with the business-necessity defense to disparate impact; a BFOQ openly uses a protected trait.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-talent-003.explanation: BFOQ is narrow. This item asks: “A BFOQ is:”. The matching answer is: A rare, legally allowed sex/religion/national-origin requirement that is essential to the job. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. It is rare and narrowly construed.

options.a: A check that each protected group's pass rate is at least 50% of the highest group's
options.b: A review of test content by managers, since statistics are used only after a lawsuit
options.c: A count of protected-class hires per year, with validation needed for any shortfall
options.d: A statistical look at pass rates by protected class, then a validity defense if needed

distractorExplanations.a: Wrong threshold: the UGESP screen is the four-fifths (80%) rule, not 50%.
distractorExplanations.b: Employers are expected to monitor selection rates proactively under UGESP, not only once litigation starts.
distractorExplanations.c: Adverse impact compares selection rates, not raw hire counts against a quota.

options.a: Role, tools, compliance, and a 30-day check
options.b: Benefits forms and a signed handbook receipt
options.c: Company history and culture, with role training at 90 days
options.d: A full-day compliance video before meeting the manager

distractorExplanations.b: Paperwork is orientation, not onboarding; it leaves out role clarity, tools, and an early check-in.
distractorExplanations.c: Delaying role training to 90 days slows time-to-productivity; culture content alone is not onboarding.
distractorExplanations.d: Compliance content matters, but onboarding centers on the role and manager connection, not a video day.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-talent-005.explanation: Time-to-productivity is a metric. This item asks: “Onboarding should include:”. The matching answer is: Role, tools, compliance, and a 30-day check — not a handbook toss. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. A handbook alone is not onboarding.

options.a: The test measures the wrong construct for the job
options.b: Scores bounce — you cannot trust the rank order
options.c: The test has adverse impact on a protected group
options.d: Scores are consistent but do not predict performance

distractorExplanations.a: Measuring the wrong construct is a validity problem; reliability is about consistency of scores.
distractorExplanations.c: Adverse impact concerns group pass-rate differences, a separate issue from score consistency.
distractorExplanations.d: This describes a reliable but invalid test, the reverse of a reliability problem.

options.a: Scores correlate with later job performance
options.b: The sample measures an abstract trait
options.c: The sample mirrors important job tasks
options.d: Retesting gives the same scores over time

distractorExplanations.a: Correlation with later performance is criterion-related validity, not content validity.
distractorExplanations.b: Measuring an abstract trait is construct validity; content validity samples actual job tasks.
distractorExplanations.d: Stable scores on retest describe test-retest reliability, not content validity.

options.a: Ranked by salary, highest first
options.b: Based on manager gut sense of fit
options.c: Kept confidential from legal review
options.d: Job-related and documented

distractorExplanations.a: Cutting top earners first often tracks age and can create ADEA disparate-impact exposure.
distractorExplanations.b: Subjective 'fit' is undocumented and hard to defend against discrimination claims.
distractorExplanations.c: RIF lists should get legal and adverse-impact review before notices go out.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-talent-008.explanation: Document the criteria. This item asks: “A RIF selection list should be:”. The matching answer is: Job-related and documented, not a secret 'attitude' sort. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Avoid secret 'attitude' sorts.

options.a: Postings are real and managers do not hide roles
options.b: Roles go to manager referrals before posting
options.c: Transfers are capped so top performers stay in their teams
options.d: Openings go to the external market first to test the pay

distractorExplanations.b: Filling roles by referral before posting closes the internal market and undermines trust.
distractorExplanations.c: Capping transfers is talent hoarding, a main reason internal mobility programs fail.
distractorExplanations.d: Going external first sidelines internal candidates; mobility needs real internal access.

options.a: Raise offer acceptance by highlighting only the perks
options.b: Cut early turnover by telling the hard parts too
options.c: Screen out applicants who fail a knowledge test
options.d: Replace the formal job description during onboarding

distractorExplanations.a: That is a sales pitch; an RJP deliberately shares the downsides so candidates can self-select.
distractorExplanations.c: Knowledge testing is a selection tool; an RJP relies on candidate self-selection, not a test.
distractorExplanations.d: An RJP supplements the job description during recruiting; it does not replace it.

options.a: Section 1 within 3 business days of the start date
options.b: Required only for employees who are not U.S. citizens
options.c: Section 1 by day 1, documents timed
options.d: Completed for new hires after their 90-day probation

distractorExplanations.a: Swaps the deadlines: Section 1 is due by the first day; three business days is the Section 2 deadline.
distractorExplanations.b: Every new hire, including U.S. citizens, must complete Form I-9.
distractorExplanations.d: The I-9 is due at hire (Section 1 day 1, Section 2 within three business days), not after probation.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-talent-011.explanation: IRCA timing is real. This item asks: “I-9 completion is:”. The matching answer is: Section 1 by day 1, documents timed — not 'whenever payroll remembers'. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Section 2 documents are reviewed within three business days of the start date.

options.a: Identifying and developing backups for critical roles
options.b: Choosing the next CEO by board vote when the role opens
options.c: A replacement chart listing names with no development plan
options.d: Forecasting total headcount needs for the next fiscal year

distractorExplanations.b: Waiting until a role opens is reactive replacement; succession planning prepares candidates in advance.
distractorExplanations.c: A replacement chart without development is only a list; succession planning builds readiness.
distractorExplanations.d: Headcount forecasting is workforce planning; succession focuses on backups for critical roles.

options.a: A single structured interview with a trained panel
options.b: Multiple job-like exercises rated on competencies
options.c: A cognitive ability test scored against national norms
options.d: An off-site training center for high-potential leaders

distractorExplanations.a: A structured interview is one method; an assessment center combines several job-like exercises.
distractorExplanations.c: A cognitive test is a single paper measure, not multiple simulations rated by assessors.
distractorExplanations.d: Despite the name, an assessment center is an evaluation method, not a training facility.

options.a: The official HRCI PHR exam form licensed for practice
options.b: An SHRM-CP practice set relabeled for PHR candidates
options.c: Independent HRCI-style practice — not the official PHR
options.d: The HRCI aPHR exam, which this mock replaces

distractorExplanations.a: HRCI does not license live exam forms; this is independent practice, not the official PHR.
distractorExplanations.b: SHRM-CP is a different credential from a different body; this mock follows the HRCI PHR outline.
distractorExplanations.d: The aPHR is HRCI's entry-level credential; this independent mock neither is nor replaces any HRCI exam.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-talent-015.explanation: Different body. This item asks: “This PHR mock is:”. The matching answer is: Independent HRCI-style practice — not the official PHR and not SHRM-CP. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. It is also not SHRM-CP.

options.a: Summarize the employee's attitude and personality traits
options.b: Be kept in a manager's private file the employee does not see
options.c: Issue a final warning so the employee knows it is serious
options.d: State the gap, the expectation, and the follow-up date

distractorExplanations.a: Documentation should describe observable behavior and results, not attitude or personality labels.
distractorExplanations.b: Secret files undercut fairness; the employee should know what was discussed and expected.
distractorExplanations.c: Coaching is an early step; jumping to a final warning skips progressive discipline.

options.a: The conduct is egregious and policy allows summary action
options.b: The employee has already received one verbal warning
options.c: The manager has documented two minor attendance issues
options.d: The employee files a complaint shortly before discipline

distractorExplanations.b: One prior verbal warning is the normal next step in progression, not grounds to skip to termination.
distractorExplanations.c: Minor attendance issues call for progressive steps, not summary action.
distractorExplanations.d: Skipping steps right after a complaint creates retaliation risk; protected activity is never a reason to accelerate.

options.a: Any non-union employee's right to bring a lawyer to a meeting
options.b: A union employee's request for a rep in an investigatory interview
options.c: A union's right to bargain over a disciplinary policy change
options.d: A union employee's right to a rep at any routine work meeting

distractorExplanations.a: Weingarten covers union representatives for unionized employees; it gives no right to bring a lawyer.
distractorExplanations.c: Bargaining over policy changes is a separate NLRA duty, not the Weingarten interview right.
distractorExplanations.d: Weingarten applies to investigatory interviews the employee reasonably believes may lead to discipline, not routine meetings.

options.a: Wait until a second complaint confirms a pattern
options.b: Be run by the accused employee's own manager
options.c: Be prompt, impartial, and documented
options.d: Promise the complainant total confidentiality

distractorExplanations.a: Employers must act promptly on the first complaint; waiting for a pattern weakens the Faragher/Ellerth defense.
distractorExplanations.b: The accused's own manager has a conflict of interest; investigators must be impartial.
distractorExplanations.d: Confidentiality can be kept as far as possible, but total confidentiality cannot be promised in an investigation.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-employee-rel-01.explanation: Process protects everyone. This item asks: “An investigation of harassment should:”. The matching answer is: Be prompt, impartial, and documented — not a gossip circle. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Avoid a gossip circle.

options.a: Terminating without giving a reason in writing
options.b: Firing an employee for poor performance without warnings
options.c: Changing duties or schedules without employee consent
options.d: Firing for a discriminatory or retaliatory reason

distractorExplanations.a: At-will employers generally need not give a written reason, though some states require service letters.
distractorExplanations.b: At-will allows termination for performance without progressive warnings unless a contract or policy says otherwise.
distractorExplanations.c: At-will employers can usually change duties and schedules, subject to contracts and specific laws.

options.a: A written final boundary before termination
options.b: A verbal warning given before written discipline
options.c: A severance contract that waives future claims
options.d: A performance plan with no consequence

distractorExplanations.b: A verbal warning is the first step of progressive discipline, not the final written boundary.
distractorExplanations.c: A severance agreement follows separation; a last-chance agreement keeps the employee on clear terms.
distractorExplanations.d: A last-chance agreement states that a further violation leads to termination; no consequence defeats its purpose.

options.a: They let employees file grievances outside the policy
options.b: They surface issues without undermining the manager
options.c: They replace regular one-on-ones with the direct manager
options.d: Results stay with the senior leader, not shared with HR

distractorExplanations.a: Skip-levels are listening sessions; formal complaints still follow the grievance or complaint policy.
distractorExplanations.c: Skip-levels supplement direct-manager one-on-ones; replacing them undermines the manager.
distractorExplanations.d: Themes should be shared with HR so patterns are acted on, not kept by one leader.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-employee-rel-02.explanation: Design them. This item asks: “Skip-level meetings help when:”. The matching answer is: They surface issues without undermining the manager as policy. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Design them as a policy, not a complaint dump.

options.a: The company open-door policy
options.b: An NLRB unfair labor practice charge
options.c: The contractual path
options.d: A manager-designed appeal process

distractorExplanations.a: An open-door policy is a non-union tool; in a union shop, grievances follow the CBA procedure.
distractorExplanations.b: ULP charges go to the NLRB for statutory violations; contract disputes go through the CBA grievance steps.
distractorExplanations.d: Management cannot replace the bargained grievance procedure with its own appeal process.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-employee-rel-02.explanation: Follow the CBA. This item asks: “A grievance procedure in a union shop is:”. The matching answer is: The contractual path — do not freelance a different process. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Do not freelance a different process.

options.a: Tie manager bonuses to raising the scores
options.b: Share the scores and move to next year
options.c: Survey monthly to track every small change
options.d: Act on a few drivers and close the loop

distractorExplanations.a: Paying for scores invites gaming and pressure on respondents instead of fixing the drivers.
distractorExplanations.b: Sharing without action breeds survey cynicism; the value comes from acting and reporting back.
distractorExplanations.c: More frequent surveys without action add fatigue, not engagement.

options.a: Manage conflicts and harassment risk
options.b: Ban relationships between any two employees
options.c: Replace sexual harassment training for managers
options.d: Require HR approval before employees date

distractorExplanations.b: Most policies target supervisor-subordinate conflicts; blanket bans are hard to enforce and can raise privacy issues.
distractorExplanations.c: A romance policy complements harassment training; it does not replace it.
distractorExplanations.d: Policies usually require disclosure of relationships in a reporting line, not prior HR approval to date.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-employee-rel-02.explanation: Disclose reporting lines. This item asks: “A workplace romance policy is meant to:”. The matching answer is: Manage conflicts and harassment risk, not ban all friendship. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. It is not a ban on all friendship.

options.a: Disagreeing with a manager in a meeting
options.b: A clear refusal of a lawful work order
options.c: Refusing an order that violates OSHA safety rules
options.d: Missing a deadline because of workload

distractorExplanations.a: Respectful disagreement is not refusal; insubordination requires refusing a lawful directive.
distractorExplanations.c: Refusing work that poses imminent danger can be protected under OSHA; it is not insubordination.
distractorExplanations.d: A missed deadline is a performance issue, not a refusal of an order.

options.a: A promise of rehire priority to keep the meeting calm
options.b: A waiver with 7 days to consider for employees over 40 in a group RIF
options.c: The business reason, the date, and the benefits/WARN pieces that apply
options.d: A WARN notice handed over on the day of the layoff

distractorExplanations.a: Unplanned rehire promises can create contract claims; stick to the documented reason and benefits.
distractorExplanations.b: OWBPA gives employees 40+ in a group program 45 days to consider and 7 days to revoke; 7 days is the revocation period.
distractorExplanations.d: WARN requires 60 days' advance notice for covered layoffs, not notice on the day of the layoff.

options.a: A small style clash
options.b: A missed email tone
options.c: A dispute over shift swaps
options.d: Harassment or violence

distractorExplanations.c: Scheduling disputes between peers are a good fit for mediation; harassment and violence require investigation.
distractorExplanations.a: “A small style clash” does not answer “Peer mediation is a bad fit for:”. The matching answer is: Harassment or violence — use investigation.
distractorExplanations.b: “A missed email tone” does not answer “Peer mediation is a bad fit for:”. The matching answer is: Harassment or violence — use investigation.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-employee-rel-02.explanation: Do not mediate abuse. This item asks: “Peer mediation is a bad fit for:”. The matching answer is: Harassment or violence — use investigation. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. These require a formal investigation, not mediation.

options.a: Punish protected leave the same as no-call no-show
options.b: Assign points for unexcused absences and tardies
options.c: Reset points after a period of good attendance
options.d: Require call-in before the start of a shift

distractorExplanations.b: Pointing unexcused absences is the normal design; the failure is pointing protected leave.
distractorExplanations.c: Rolling resets are a common, lawful feature that rewards improved attendance.
distractorExplanations.d: Call-in rules are lawful and can apply to FMLA users under usual procedures.

options.a: Rejected until the employee gives two weeks' notice
options.b: Confirmed in writing with last day and access cutoff
options.c: Processed as a termination for cause to block benefits
options.d: Accepted verbally with access kept through the last paycheck

distractorExplanations.a: Two weeks' notice is a courtesy; at-will employees can resign without it being accepted.
distractorExplanations.c: Recasting a resignation as a for-cause firing without facts is inaccurate and creates legal risk.
distractorExplanations.d: Access should be cut on the last day, not left open until the final paycheck; confirm in writing.

options.a: An incumbent's performance rating and years of service in the role
options.b: The market rate for the job from salary surveys
options.c: A job-related dimension like skill, effort, responsibility, conditions
options.d: The employee's education credentials beyond job needs

distractorExplanations.a: Performance and tenure describe the person; compensable factors evaluate the job.
distractorExplanations.b: Market rates are used in market pricing; point-factor plans rate internal job dimensions.
distractorExplanations.d: Factors measure what the job requires, not credentials an incumbent holds beyond it.

options.a: 1.5× after 8 hours in any workday
options.b: 2× after 40 hours in the workweek
options.c: 1.5× after 80 hours in a two-week period
options.d: 1.5× after 40 hours in the workweek

distractorExplanations.a: Daily overtime after 8 hours is a state rule (e.g., California), not the federal FLSA standard.
distractorExplanations.b: The FLSA rate is 1.5×; double time comes from state law or company policy.
distractorExplanations.c: The 8/80 system is a limited exception for hospitals and residential care facilities, not the usual rule.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-comp-ben-032.explanation: Hours are hours. This item asks: “FLSA overtime for a nonexempt is:”. The matching answer is: 1.5× after 40 hours in the workweek (usual federal rule). Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. This is the usual federal rule.

options.a: Meet duties and salary tests
options.b: Hold a manager or director title
options.c: Earn a salary, with duties not reviewed
options.d: Supervise at least five full-time employees

distractorExplanations.b: A title alone does not make anyone exempt; actual duties and salary decide.
distractorExplanations.c: Salary basis is only one test; the duties test must also be met.
distractorExplanations.d: The executive exemption requires directing at least two full-time employees, not five.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-comp-ben-033.explanation: Duties tests matter. This item asks: “An exempt EAP employee still must:”. The matching answer is: Meet duties and salary tests — a title is not enough. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. A title is not enough.

options.a: Pay is 80% of the range maximum
options.b: Pay is at 80% of range midpoint
options.c: Pay is 20% above the range midpoint
options.d: Pay is at the 80th market percentile

distractorExplanations.a: Compa-ratio divides pay by the range midpoint, not the maximum.
distractorExplanations.c: Reverses the direction: 0.80 is 20% below the midpoint, not above.
distractorExplanations.d: A percentile is a market position; compa-ratio is pay ÷ midpoint of the range.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-comp-ben-034.explanation: Read the range. This item asks: “A compa-ratio of 0.80 means:”. The matching answer is: Pay is at 80% of range midpoint — a signal, not a crime by itself. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. It is a signal to review, not a violation by itself.

options.a: You want to minimize fixed labor costs
options.b: Turnover is low and roles are easy to fill
options.c: You need scarce talent and can fund it
options.d: The labor market is soft and budgets are tight

distractorExplanations.a: Minimizing labor costs points to a lag-the-market strategy, not a lead strategy.
distractorExplanations.b: Low turnover and easy-to-fill roles argue for meeting or lagging the market.
distractorExplanations.d: A soft market and tight budget favor lagging; leading costs more.

options.a: Excluded from federal income tax withholding as a gift to staff
options.b: Included in the FLSA regular rate used to calculate overtime pay
options.c: Owed to departing employees under final paycheck laws
options.d: Not a guaranteed wage in the same way a promised commission may be

distractorExplanations.a: Bonuses are taxable supplemental wages subject to withholding, not gifts.
distractorExplanations.b: Reversed: truly discretionary bonuses are excluded from the regular rate; nondiscretionary bonuses are included.
distractorExplanations.c: Final-pay laws cover earned wages; a truly discretionary bonus is generally not an earned wage owed at exit.

options.a: Continuation of group health after qualifying events
options.b: Conversion of group life insurance to an individual policy
options.c: Retiree health coverage funded by a pension plan
options.d: Health coverage portability rules for preexisting conditions

distractorExplanations.b: Life insurance conversion is a policy feature; COBRA covers group health plans.
distractorExplanations.c: COBRA is temporary, employee-paid continuation, not retiree coverage funded by a pension.
distractorExplanations.d: Portability and preexisting-condition rules came from HIPAA, not COBRA.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-comp-ben-037.explanation: Qualifying events. This item asks: “COBRA is about:”. The matching answer is: Continuation of group health after qualifying events, at a cost. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Coverage continues at the participant's cost (up to 102% of premium).

options.a: Guaranteeing participants a minimum annual return
options.b: Prudent process and fees that can be explained
options.c: Picking the cheapest funds without other review
options.d: Matching employee deferrals at the IRS maximum

distractorExplanations.a: ERISA judges fiduciaries on prudent process, not on guaranteeing investment results.
distractorExplanations.c: Low fees matter, but prudence weighs quality and suitability too, not cost alone.
distractorExplanations.d: Matching formulas are a plan design choice, not a fiduciary duty.

options.a: Filed with the DOL in place of the Form 5500
options.b: Given to participants only when they request it
options.c: Understandable and given on the ERISA timeline
options.d: Written as the full legal plan document itself

distractorExplanations.a: SPDs are no longer routinely filed with the DOL, and they never replace the Form 5500 annual report.
distractorExplanations.b: ERISA requires automatic distribution to participants within set deadlines, not only on request.
distractorExplanations.d: The SPD summarizes the plan in plain language; the plan document is a separate instrument.

options.a: Lose its HSA eligibility under IRS rules
options.b: Violate FLSA overtime and minimum wage rules
options.c: Require OSHA injury recordkeeping
options.d: Create ADA/GINA/HIPAA problems

distractorExplanations.a: HSA eligibility depends on the health plan design, not on wellness incentive pressure.
distractorExplanations.b: Wellness coercion raises ADA voluntariness and GINA issues, not FLSA wage problems.
distractorExplanations.c: OSHA recordkeeping covers work injuries; it is not triggered by wellness program design.

options.a: Replace the annual W-2 form
options.b: Show pay plus benefits value
options.c: Report benefits costs to the IRS
options.d: Determine each job's FLSA status

distractorExplanations.a: A total rewards statement is a communication tool; the W-2 is a required tax form.
distractorExplanations.c: Benefit costs reported to the IRS go on the W-2 or other filings, not a total rewards statement.
distractorExplanations.d: FLSA status comes from duties and salary tests, not a rewards statement.

options.a: Overtime pay required for night work
options.b: Premium pay set by FLSA for weekend shifts
options.c: Extra pay for less desirable hours
options.d: A bonus paid for perfect attendance

distractorExplanations.a: The FLSA requires no extra pay for night work; shift differentials are voluntary.
distractorExplanations.b: The FLSA does not mandate weekend premiums; any premium comes from policy or contract.
distractorExplanations.d: Attendance bonuses reward attendance, not working less desirable shifts.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-comp-ben-043.explanation: Define it in policy. This item asks: “Shift differential is:”. The matching answer is: Extra pay for less desirable hours, if you offer it. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. It applies if the employer offers it.

options.a: It is excluded from taxable wages
options.b: It is taxed only when paid in cash
options.c: It is reported on a 1099-NEC
options.d: The IRS may tax a portion

distractorExplanations.a: Imputed income is the taxable value of a noncash benefit; it is added to wages.
distractorExplanations.b: Imputed income applies to noncash benefits, such as group-term life over $50,000.
distractorExplanations.c: Employee imputed income is reported on the W-2; Form 1099-NEC is for nonemployee compensation.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-comp-ben-044.explanation: Tax is part of benefits. This item asks: “Imputed income on a benefit means:”. The matching answer is: The IRS may tax a portion — payroll has to get it right. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Payroll has to get it right.

options.a: A contract/policy tool
options.b: An FLSA overtime offset
options.c: A COBRA qualifying event
options.d: A remedy only for public companies

distractorExplanations.b: Clawbacks recover incentive pay after misconduct; they are not tied to FLSA overtime.
distractorExplanations.c: COBRA qualifying events trigger health continuation, not bonus recovery.
distractorExplanations.d: SEC/Dodd-Frank rules require clawbacks at listed companies, but private employers can adopt them by contract too.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-comp-ben-045.explanation: Write it first. This item asks: “A clawback on a bonus after fraud is:”. The matching answer is: A contract/policy tool — draft it before you need it. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Draft it before you need it.

options.a: Race, color, sex, age, and disability
options.b: Race, color, religion, sex, national origin
options.c: Race, religion, sex, and veteran status
options.d: Color, religion, national origin, and genetics

distractorExplanations.a: Age is protected by the ADEA and disability by the ADA, not Title VII.
distractorExplanations.c: Veteran status is protected by USERRA/VEVRAA; the list also omits color and national origin.
distractorExplanations.d: Genetic information is protected by GINA, and the list omits race and sex.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-compliance-046.explanation: Know the statute. This item asks: “Title VII covers:”. The matching answer is: Race, color, religion, sex, national origin — and the case law on harassment/retaliation. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Case law extends it to harassment and retaliation.

options.a: A medical exam the employer orders first
options.b: A review limited to the employee's job title
options.c: A dialogue about reasonable accommodation
options.d: An undue-hardship denial issued in writing

distractorExplanations.a: Employers may request reasonable documentation, but the process is a dialogue, not a mandatory exam first.
distractorExplanations.b: The process looks at the person's limitations and essential functions, not just the title.
distractorExplanations.d: Undue hardship is a defense considered after exploring options, not the process itself.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-compliance-047.explanation: Talk, then decide. This item asks: “ADA interactive process is:”. The matching answer is: A dialogue about reasonable accommodation, not a one-letter deny. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. It is not a one-letter denial.

options.a: 6 months, 1,000 hours, and 15 or more employees
options.b: 12 months, 1,000 hours, and 20 employees at the site
options.c: 12 months of service, with no hours threshold
options.d: 12 months, 1250 hours, and a covered employer size

distractorExplanations.a: Uses ADA/Title VII-like figures; FMLA requires 12 months, 1,250 hours, and 50 employees within 75 miles.
distractorExplanations.b: 1,000 hours is the ERISA vesting year; FMLA requires 1,250 hours and 50 employees within 75 miles.
distractorExplanations.c: FMLA has both a 12-month and a 1,250-hour test in the prior 12 months.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-compliance-048.explanation: Do the math. This item asks: “FMLA eligible employee typically needs:”. The matching answer is: 12 months, 1250 hours, and a covered employer size — then a qualifying reason. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. A qualifying reason is also needed.

options.a: OSHA recordkeeping for work-related injuries
options.b: The OSHA annual summary posted Feb–Apr
options.c: The OSHA incident report for each case
options.d: A workers' comp claim form for the insurer

distractorExplanations.b: The annual summary posted February 1 to April 30 is Form 300A, not the 300 log.
distractorExplanations.c: The detailed incident report for each case is Form 301.
distractorExplanations.d: Workers' comp claims are state insurance forms, separate from OSHA logs.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-compliance-049.explanation: Recordables have tests. This item asks: “A Form 300 log is:”. The matching answer is: OSHA recordkeeping for work-related injuries that meet the criteria. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Only cases that meet recording criteria go on the log.

options.a: Paid military leave for up to 5 years
options.b: Reemployment rights after uniformed service
options.c: Rehire only if the employee gave 30 days' notice
options.d: Unpaid leave limited to 12 weeks per year

distractorExplanations.a: USERRA protects up to 5 cumulative years of service, but the leave is generally unpaid.
distractorExplanations.c: USERRA requires advance notice where possible, with no 30-day minimum.
distractorExplanations.d: Twelve weeks per year is the FMLA limit; USERRA covers up to 5 cumulative years.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-compliance-050.explanation: Military leave is federal. This item asks: “USERRA requires:”. The matching answer is: Reemployment rights after uniformed service as the statute says. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Reemployment applies as the statute describes.

options.a: Run a job-related background check for a driver role
options.b: Skip a check for a desk role with no safety duties
options.c: Skip a reasonable check for a role with foreseeable harm
options.d: Follow FCRA steps before taking adverse action

distractorExplanations.a: A job-related check lowers negligent-hire risk rather than raising it.
distractorExplanations.b: With no foreseeable harm, skipping a check carries less risk than skipping one for a high-risk role.
distractorExplanations.d: FCRA compliance governs how checks are used; it reduces, not raises, negligent-hire risk.

options.a: Medical exams after a conditional job offer
options.b: Questions about an applicant's age or birth date
options.c: Use of drug test results in hiring decisions
options.d: Genetic information in employment decisions

distractorExplanations.a: Post-offer medical exams are governed by the ADA, not GINA.
distractorExplanations.b: Questions about age or birth date raise ADEA concerns; GINA covers genetic information and family medical history.
distractorExplanations.c: Drug tests are not medical exams under the ADA and are not genetic information under GINA.

options.a: A spreadsheet of SSNs to the wrong vendor
options.b: A redacted headcount report to the CFO
options.c: A job posting to an external job board
options.d: A benefits guide link to all employees

distractorExplanations.b: Redacted aggregate data to an authorized executive is not a privacy breach.
distractorExplanations.c: A job posting is public information meant for outside audiences, so emailing it exposes no personal data.
distractorExplanations.d: A general benefits guide contains no individual personal data.

options.a: Paying every employee in a role the range midpoint
options.b: Posting ranges and not retaliating for pay talk
options.c: Disclosing each employee's salary publicly
options.d: Banning salary discussions among coworkers

distractorExplanations.a: Transparency laws require disclosure of ranges, not paying everyone the midpoint.
distractorExplanations.c: Laws require posting ranges for roles, not publishing individual salaries.
distractorExplanations.d: Banning pay discussions conflicts with NLRA Section 7 and many transparency laws.

options.a: A pay equity audit filed with the OFCCP
options.b: Optional for a 10,000-person federal contractor
options.c: A demographic report to the EEOC on the timeline
options.d: An affirmative action plan filed with the DOL

distractorExplanations.a: The EEO-1 reports workforce demographics to the EEOC; it is not a pay equity audit for OFCCP.
distractorExplanations.d: Affirmative action plans are kept by contractors, not filed as the EEO-1 report.
distractorExplanations.b: “Optional for a 10,000-person federal contractor always” does not answer “An EEO-1 (when you must file) is:”. The matching answer is: A demographic report to the EEOC on the timeline.

options.a: Abatement
options.b: An investigation
options.c: Better guarding
options.d: Retaliation

distractorExplanations.a: Abatement (fixing the hazard) is the proper response; OSH Act Section 11(c) bars retaliation.
distractorExplanations.b: “An investigation” does not answer “A workplace safety complaint to OSHA that is real should not be met with:”. The matching answer is: Retaliation.
distractorExplanations.c: “Better guarding” does not answer “A workplace safety complaint to OSHA that is real should not be met with:”. The matching answer is: Retaliation.

options.a: The statutory later-of rule
options.b: Three years after the hire date
options.c: One year after termination
options.d: Seven years after termination

distractorExplanations.b: Three years after hire is only half of the rule; the later of that or one year after termination applies.
distractorExplanations.c: One year after termination is half of the rule; use whichever date is later.
distractorExplanations.d: Seven years is a common tax-record habit, not the I-9 rule.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-compliance-057.explanation: Count the years. This item asks: “Record retention for I-9s is:”. The matching answer is: The statutory later-of rule — not 'until the drawer is full'. Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. Keep I-9s 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination, whichever is later.

options.a: Employment is promised for at least one year
options.b: The handbook is not a contract
options.c: Policies change only with employee consent
options.d: Discipline will follow every listed step

distractorExplanations.a: A guarantee of term employment destroys at-will status; the disclaimer should do the opposite.
distractorExplanations.c: Disclaimers usually reserve the employer's right to change policies; requiring consent creates contract terms.
distractorExplanations.d: Promising every step can create an implied contract for progressive discipline.

phr-hrci-readiness-check-compliance-058.explanation: Words create contracts. This item asks: “A handbook disclaimer should say:”. The matching answer is: The handbook is not a contract (where you want at-will preserved). Independent UniPrep diagnostic — not an official HRCI PHR paper. This preserves at-will employment where desired.

options.a: Follow federal law, which preempts state
options.b: Apply the federal rule to exempt staff
options.c: Follow the stricter rule that applies
options.d: Average the two rules for each employee

distractorExplanations.a: Federal employment laws generally set a floor; more protective state laws are not preempted.
distractorExplanations.b: Exempt status is an FLSA wage concept; it does not remove state sick-leave rights.
distractorExplanations.d: Employers follow the more protective rule, not an average.

options.a: A shield that keeps the underlying facts out of discovery
options.b: Created when HR stamps notes 'privileged'
options.c: A reason to deny the accused any chance to respond
options.d: Not a reason to skip a fair process for the employee

distractorExplanations.a: Privilege protects attorney-client communications, not the underlying facts.
distractorExplanations.b: A label does not create privilege; it requires legal advice from counsel.
distractorExplanations.c: Privilege does not remove the need for a fair process that lets the accused respond.
